notes:
Circuit: a 10A current source feeding three parallel branches hung between one top node and one grounded bottom node. Branch A (x~405): 2H inductor -> 1Ohm resistor -> 10MF capacitor. Branch B (x~546): 3H inductor -> 1Ohm resistor. Branch C: the 10Ohm resistor (x~680) in parallel with the 10V source (x~840), the pair spanning the same two nodes. The drafter drew the top node as a staircase of three offset horizontal runs (y~187, y~210, y~260, y~348) linked by short vertical drops at x~487, x~638 and x~766, and the bottom node as a staircase at y~588, y~652, y~726, y~758 linked by drops at x~744 and x~625. 9 components, 5 nets.

NET MAP
  0  = bottom node / ground. From the 10A source's bottom lead (2.1 at (197,491)) down to y~740 and right along the lowest rail through S13 (473,726) and S15 (470,758) into the GND symbol (8.0 at (470,776)); the 10MF capacitor's bottom plate (7.1 at (402,567)) drops down the x~403 column to that same rail; east of S13 the rail rises at x~625 to S12 (625,652), where the y~652 run goes left to the bottom of the 1Ohm resistor #6 (6.1 at (542,550), reached by its 185px lead) and right to x~744, rising at S9 (744,590) onto the y~588 run, which goes left to the bottom of the 10Ohm resistor (5.1 at (680,523)) and right to the bottom of the 10V source (4.0 at (829,524)).
  n1 = top node. From the 10A source's top lead (2.0 at (213,330)) up to y~187, right to x~487, down to S0 (487,209); the y~210 run goes left to the 2H inductor top (0.0 at (401,236)) and right to x~638, down at S4 (638,261) onto the y~260 run, which goes left to the 3H inductor top (1.0 at (544,292)) and right to x~766, down at S6 (766,352) onto the y~348 run, which goes left to the 10Ohm resistor top (5.0 at (680,404)) and right to x~855 then down to the 10V source top (4.1 at (849,402)). Five terminals in all.
  n2 = 2H inductor bottom (0.1 at (409,355)) to the top of the 1Ohm resistor #3 (3.0 at (404,369)) -- the short x~405 column between them.
  n3 = 3H inductor bottom (1.1 at (550,424)) to the top of the 1Ohm resistor #6 (6.0 at (547,438)) -- the short x~548 column between them.
  n4 = bottom of the 1Ohm resistor #3 to the top plate of the 10MF capacitor -- the x~403 column between y=479 (bottom edge of #3's box) and y=488 (top edge of #7's box). Two terminals only; see MERGE below.

JUDGEMENT CALLS (all seven CRITICAL sites; tracer default accepted at each, recorded explicitly). Every one is a deg=3 T where a run terminates on a continuous run -- there is no 4-way plain X anywhere on the wire graph of this sheet, so there was no junction-vs-crossing ambiguity to resolve on any net-changing site.
  S0 (487,209) JUNCTION. The y~187 rail from the current source turns down at x~487 and lands on the y~210 rail, which continues both left (to the 2H inductor) and right (towards S4). Crossing is not expressible here -- the incoming run terminates. Any non-junction reading would cut the 10A source off from all three branches.
  S4 (638,261) JUNCTION. Same shape one step down the staircase: the y~210 rail curves down at x~638 and terminates on the y~260 rail, which continues left to the 3H inductor and right towards S6. A non-junction reading would split the top node in two and strand the 3H branch and the 10Ohm/10V pair.
  S6 (766,352) JUNCTION. The x~766 vertical drops from y~260 and terminates on the y~348 rail, which runs left to the 10Ohm resistor top and right to the 10V source top. A non-junction reading would leave the 10Ohm/10V pair floating at the top.
  S9 (744,590) JUNCTION. The y~588 rail runs left-right (10Ohm bottom to 10V bottom) and a vertical leaves it downward at x~744 towards S12. Crossing would leave the 10Ohm/10V pair with no return to the source.
  S12 (625,652) JUNCTION. The y~652 rail runs left-right (1Ohm #6 bottom to the S9 drop) with a vertical leaving downward at x~625 towards S13. Crossing would disconnect the whole right half of the bottom node from ground.
  S13 (473,726) JUNCTION. The y~726 rail runs left-right; a vertical leaves downward at x~473 and the y~758 rail (from the current source's bottom) joins the same vertical just below. Crossing would separate the source's return from the branch returns and the ground.
  S15 (470,758) JUNCTION. The y~758 rail from the current source's bottom terminates on the x~470 vertical, which continues down into the GND symbol at (470,776). Crossing would leave the entire circuit ungrounded.

NON-CRITICAL SITE (left at default): S8 (334,551), deg=4, default 'crossing' with hop score 9.5 -- this is the descender of the 'F' in the '10MF' caption running across the lower capacitor plate. Label ink, not wire; it does not change the netlist either way.

MERGE (one; this is a bounding-box occlusion, not a faded line)
  ['3.1','7.0'] joins the bottom of the 1Ohm resistor #3 to the top plate of the 10MF capacitor #7. The two annotated boxes are only 9 px apart (#3 spans y 374..479, #7 spans y 488..563 at overlapping x), so when the tracer deleted both boxes the connecting wire was reduced to a 4-pixel orphan stub -- edges.py at (404,490) r=40 returns exactly one edge, e17, len=4 from (405,482) to (403,484), touching no site, which was then dropped as an orphan. Neither terminal had a usable port left: resistor #3's remaining candidates p0 (439,404) and p1 (440,436) are both strokes of the '1 Ohm' caption written to its right, and capacitor #7's candidates p1 (344,533) and p2 (344,550) are both strokes of the '10MF' caption written to its left. That produced the two one-terminal nets n4 and n5. I verified the real ink with inkmap.py at (404,483) win=22: an unbroken 4-px-wide vertical column of '#' at x=402..405 runs continuously from y=461 through y=505, straight through the gap between the two boxes. The two terminals are therefore genuinely one node, and merging them gives a correct 2-terminal net; 'ports' could not reach either terminal because no port sits on the real lead. Both single-terminal warnings clear.

CLASSES: all nine match the drawing -- two coiled inductors (2H, 3H), three zig-zag resistors (1Ohm at x~400, 1Ohm at x~545, 10Ohm at x~680), a two-plate capacitor (10MF) drawn with horizontal plates and vertical leads, a circle-with-up-arrow I-DC (10A), a circle-with-plus/minus V-DC (10V) and the ladder GND. Nothing to reclassify.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. The only non-trivial call was the resistor-to-capacitor merge, verified in the pixels above.
